traceability.evidence:
Implementation and tests for Story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md are present and passing:
- Core rules: - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts - File-level JSDoc: @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and @req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED. - Uses helpers from src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts and src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts. - meta.messages.missingStory gives an explicit, actionable message about adding @story with an example story path. - Schema defines options { scope, exportPriority } using shared DEFAULT_SCOPE and EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES. - src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts - File-level JSDoc: @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md plus @req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED, REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY. - Imports DEFAULT_SCOPE, EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES, shouldProcessNode from ./helpers/require-story-helpers for identical detection/scope/export behavior as require-story-annotation. - Calls checkReqAnnotation from src/utils/annotation-checker.ts for shared @req detection.
- Shared detection and configuration (ensuring both rules act on the same constructs): - src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts: - export const DEFAULT_SCOPE = ["FunctionDeclaration", "FunctionExpression", "MethodDefinition", "TSMethodSignature", "TSDeclareFunction"]; - export const EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES = ["all", "exported", "non-exported"]. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts: - function shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority) gates processing by node.type and export status via isExportedNode, used by both rules. - hasStoryAnnotation(...) and supporting helpers (jsdocHasStory, commentsBeforeHasStory, leadingCommentsHasStory, linesBeforeHasStory, parentChainHasStory, fallbackTextBeforeHasStory) implement robust, guarded JSDoc/comment parsing for @story. - src/utils/annotation-checker.ts and src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts: - checkReqAnnotation(context, node, options) uses getJSDocComment, getLeadingComments, getCommentsBefore, combineComments, and hasReqAnnotation(...) to detect @req in JSDoc and surrounding comments. - hasReqAnnotation reuses LOOKBACK_LINES and FALLBACK_WINDOW from require-story-io and applies line, parent-chain, and fallback text heuristics analogous to @story detection, all wrapped in try/catch for graceful failure.
- Function-like constructs & arrow exclusion (REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION): - require-story-annotation visitors (src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts) build handlers for: - FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression (skipping when parent is MethodDefinition), MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature. - ArrowFunctionExpression handler exists but is gated by options.shouldProcessNode(node); since DEFAULT_SCOPE and the scope enum do not include "ArrowFunctionExpression", arrow functions are effectively excluded by default. - require-req-annotation (src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts) defines create() listeners for the same set of node types: FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression (with MethodDefinition guard), MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature, all passed through shouldProcessNode. - Tests confirm behavior and arrow exclusion: - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts - Valid & invalid cases for all five node types above. - Explicit valid test: "[REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED] unannotated arrow function allowed by default" confirms arrow functions are not required by default. - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts - Valid/invalid coverage for FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, plus TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature via shared helpers.
- Configurable scope & export priority (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY): - Both rules expose identical schemas for options: - scope: array of node-type strings enumed from DEFAULT_SCOPE. - exportPriority: one of EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES. - Both create(context) hooks read options[0].scope and options[0].exportPriority with defaults and pass them to shouldProcessNode. - Tests validate behavior: - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts - "require-story-annotation with exportPriority option" and "with scope option" blocks verify that only in-scope/export-prioritized functions are checked. - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts - Many tests named with [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE] and [REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY] show consistent behavior for exported vs non-exported functions and methods, and for constrained scope arrays.
- Error location and UX (REQ-ERROR-LOCATION and user experience criteria): - require-story-annotation: - reportMissing and reportMethod (helpers) compute a name and choose node.id/node.key Identifiers as the report node; they pass data { name, functionName } into context.report with messageId: "missingStory". - Tests assert data.functionName for methods (e.g., method, tsDecl, etc.) in tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts. - require-req-annotation / annotation-checker: - reportMissing in src/utils/annotation-checker.ts uses getNodeName and falls back to "(anonymous)" for anonymous functions, and selects the identifier node when present. - Tests in tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts validate naming and location for named, anonymous, class, object, and TS constructs, including an anonymous FunctionExpression case expecting functionName "(anonymous)". - Messages are explicit and actionable: - missingStory message instructs adding @story and gives a concrete example path. - missingReq message instructs adding @req and gives an example identifier.
- TypeScript support (REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT): - require-story-annotation visitors for TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature call helperReportMissing; tests cover both valid and invalid TS declarations/signatures using withTsLanguageOptions. - require-req-annotation includes TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature visitors that run checkReqAnnotation; tests use runAnnotationCheckerTests (tests/utils/annotation-checker.test.ts) and withTsLanguageOptions to cover TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature (valid and invalid, including autofix via checkReqAnnotation). - Shared TS RuleTester config: - tests/utils/ts-language-options.ts defines tsRuleTesterLanguageOptions using @typescript-eslint/parser and is annotated with @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and @req REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT.
- Documentation (REQ-JSDOC-PARSING, Documentation acceptance criterion): - docs/rules/require-story-annotation.md: - References @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and @req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED. - Describes supported node types exactly as in the story and code. - Documents options scope and exportPriority with defaults and JSON schema, matching the rule implementation. - Explicitly notes that arrow functions are not currently configurable via scope, aligning with the requirement that arrow functions be excluded by default. - docs/rules/require-req-annotation.md: - References the same story and requirement and documents identical node-type coverage and options semantics, stating that semantics mirror require-story-annotation.
- Tests tied to this story with explicit traceability: - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts: - Header: "Tests for: docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md" and @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md. - Many test names embed requirement tags like [REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED], [REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION], [exportPriority], [scope]. - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts: - Header references this story and requirements REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED, REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT, and Story 007.0 for error behavior. - describe block: "Require Req Annotation Rule (Story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS)". - tests/utils/annotation-checker.test.ts also references this story in its header and uses REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT.
- Test execution evidence: - The project test script is `"test": "jest --ci --bail"` (package.json). - Tooling ran Jest with: - `npm test -- --runInBand --verbose` → executed `jest --ci --bail --runInBand --verbose` with no failure reported by the command runner. - `npm test -- --runInBand --verbose --testPathPatterns require-(story|req)-annotation` → executed `jest --ci --bail --runInBand --verbose --testPathPatterns require-(story|req)-annotation` without error, which indicates the tests specifically targeting these rules pass.
traceability.notes: The repository contains fully implemented ESLint rules require-story-annotation and require-req-annotation that align with Story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS. Both rules share a common detection model (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature), exclude arrow functions by default, and use consistent configuration (scope and exportPriority) via shared helpers. JSDoc and surrounding comment parsing is implemented robustly for both @story and @req annotations, with defensive error handling and multi-heuristic detection. Error messages are clear, actionable, and anchored at the function name (or a sensible anonymous placeholder). TypeScript-specific syntax (TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature) is supported and thoroughly tested using shared TS RuleTester configuration and helpers. Dedicated documentation for each rule matches the implemented behavior and configuration options. Comprehensive RuleTester-based test suites for these rules, explicitly tagged to this story and its requirements, run successfully under Jest. Therefore, all acceptance criteria for this story are satisfied and the story is considered implemented and passing.
